pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What Solid is, what these docs cover, and where to start reading.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.description: Go from an empty directory to a running Solid app with a change of your own in it, and meet the ideas the rest of the docs build on.

pages.title: Project shapes
pages.description: Pick between the bare, basic, and fullstack templates by what your app needs on day one, knowing that moving up later changes configuration, not your code.

pages.title: Reactivity
pages.description: Signals, memos, and effects: how Solid tracks reads, why a component runs once, and how to tell when a value will update.

pages.title: Components and JSX
pages.description: Components as functions that run once: props, children, control flow, refs, and the JSX rules that follow from that.

pages.title: Stores
pages.description: Hold a cart, a form, or any nested object in a store: update one property through a draft, derive filtered views with a projection, and load server data into the same proxy.

pages.title: Async reactivity
pages.description: Read a promise like a value: how async memos hold updates, when Loading shows a fallback, and how mutations settle.

pages.title: Boundaries
pages.description: Decide which part of the page shows a spinner, which part shows an error, and in what order regions appear, by placing Loading, Errored, and Reveal around the right subtree.

pages.title: Mutations
pages.description: Move the cart's add, remove, and set-quantity writes to a server without changing the UI: actions, optimistic stores, refresh, and how a failed request undoes itself.

pages.title: Rendering and SSR
pages.description: Run the same components in the browser and on the server: keep browser-only code off the server, get matching HTML for hydration, and choose between string and streaming rendering.

pages.title: App structure
pages.description: Know which two files in a start-mode project you edit, what the plugin generates around them, and when to replace a generated entry or hook a router into the server render.

pages.title: Styling and assets
pages.description: Style a component with global CSS, a CSS module, Tailwind, or an inline style object, toggle classes without string building, and reference images so the built URL is hashed.

pages.title: Head and metadata
pages.description: Give each page its own title and meta tags from the component that owns them, let a layout's defaults return when the page unmounts, and read a title from data that is still loading.

pages.title: Server functions
pages.description: Move a database query or a secret out of the browser by marking a function with "use server", and recognize what that call becomes on the wire.

pages.title: Reads, streams, and live data
pages.description: Declare a product read that HTTP caches can store, stream order events from a server function, and keep a stock level connected when another shopper changes it.

pages.title: Arguments and security
pages.description: Send arguments a server function can decode, and validate and authorize every call as if it came from a terminal, because it can.

pages.title: Mutations and responses
pages.description: Return a value, a redirect, a reload, or a 400 from a cart or account mutation, and control what a thrown error reveals in production.

pages.title: Metadata and transport
pages.description: Read a server-function request in the network tab, attach a header to every call, move the endpoint, and cancel one call in flight.

pages.title: Progressive enhancement
pages.description: Make the Add to cart form post to a server function before JavaScript loads, and know which part of that exchange core owns and which the router adds.

pages.title: Sessions and auth
pages.description: Build a signed cookie session on the request event, sign customers in and out from server functions, and authorize every server entry point against that session.

pages.title: Environment
pages.description: Declare environment variables once, read secrets on the server and public values in the browser through typed modules, and let the build fail when a secret would leak.

pages.title: Middleware and API routes
pages.description: Run code in front of every request with fetch-style middleware, share state with pages and server functions through the request event, and answer HTTP requests from route modules.

pages.title: Deployment
pages.description: Put a start-mode build on a host: serve dist/client as static files, route everything else to the built request handler, supply the server environment at boot, and pick a Node server or a provider adapter.

pages.title: Routing overview
pages.description: Choose between Solid Router and TanStack Router for a Solid app, mount the router in App, and decide whether routes come from an array or from files under src/routes.

pages.title: Solid Router
pages.description: Build a small routed store with Solid Router: a product page that reads its id from the URL, a header that stays mounted, typed links, and route data that starts loading before the page renders.

pages.title: Setup
pages.description: Add Solid Router to a project that does not have it, mount one router at the application root, and set the options for a base path, hash history, or preloading.

pages.title: Route definitions
pages.description: Write the route objects Solid Router matches against: path patterns with required, optional, and wildcard segments, typed parameters, match filters, metadata, lazy subtrees, and the file-system manifest.

pages.title: Nested routes and layouts
pages.description: Wrap a group of pages in a shared layout, keep it mounted while pages change, share parameters down the tree, and load data at every level without a waterfall.

pages.title: Navigation and typed paths
pages.description: Link between pages with plain anchors, build URLs the compiler checks, navigate from code, read the location and search parameters, show active and pending links, and guard against leaving a page.

pages.title: Data loading and mutations
pages.description: Start route data early with preloads, cache and share reads with query, submit mutations with actions, show optimistic state, and control what revalidates.

pages.title: Server rendering and hydration
pages.description: Render Solid Router on the server: read the URL from the request, hydrate query results without a second fetch, return fresh data from a mutation in one round trip, and keep forms working without JavaScript.

pages.title: TanStack Router
pages.description: Use TanStack Router and TanStack Query with Solid's server functions, streaming SSR, and single-flight mutations, as the fullstack-tanstack project shape does.

pages.title: Integrate a router
pages.description: Wire a router that Solid does not ship into start mode: give it the request URL and a per-request instance, and connect it to the single-flight mutation transport.

pages.title: Thinking in Solid
pages.description: Build the storefront's product search end to end, and at each step see what a React or Vue developer would reach for and what Solid does instead.

pages.title: Avoid unnecessary effects
pages.description: Recognize the effect that copies one reactive value into another, replace it with a direct, memoized, async, or writable derivation, and keep createEffect for the imperative boundary.

pages.title: Custom primitives
pages.description: Move repeated reactive setup into a createX function that runs inside an owner, accepts accessors, returns accessors, cleans up what it starts, and stays correct during server rendering.

pages.title: State management
pages.description: Decide where each piece of storefront state lives: a component, a context provider, the URL, or the server, and keep it out of module scope in code that also runs on the server.

pages.title: Forms
pages.description: Build a form with a server function and a Solid Router action: it works before JavaScript loads, validates on the server, and after hydration shows pending state, inline errors, and the saved result before the server confirms.

pages.title: Lists
pages.description: Render, edit, filter, sort, select in, and window lists without rebuilding rows, and read the diagnostics that tell you when you are.

pages.title: Data fetching patterns
pages.description: Load data for search, detail pages, pagination, shared state, and dashboards without loading flags, request counters, or abort controllers, and decide where each request and each boundary goes.

pages.title: Protected routes
pages.description: Require a signed-in customer for the account area at the data, route, and request layers, redirect a signed-out visitor to sign-in on the server and in the browser, and send them back where they were going.

pages.title: SSR-safe code
pages.description: Keep browser APIs, per-run values, and client-only data out of the server render, and read each hydration warning to find the line that made the server and the browser disagree.

pages.title: Choose a rendering mode
pages.description: Decide between a static shell, streaming server rendering, and build-time prerendering for a start-mode project, and what each one costs.

pages.title: Debugging reactivity
pages.description: Find out why a value does not update, why it updates too often, and how to read Solid's development diagnostics.

pages.title: Performance
pages.description: Measure a slow catalog page with the browser profiler and Solid's attribution tables, then fix the cause each measurement points at: hot derivations, wide writes, rebuilt rows, waterfalls, unsplit code, and a blocked streaming shell.

pages.title: TypeScript
pages.description: Replace the any annotations in a storefront with the types Solid exports for props, children, accessors, store drafts, event handlers, refs, server function results, and typed routes.

pages.title: Integrate non-Solid code
pages.description: Drive a charting library, a map, a web component, or an analytics script from Solid state: get the DOM node at the right time, create the instance once, update it in an effect, and keep browser-only imports off the server.

pages.title: Testing
pages.description: Write a component test that clicks a button and asserts the label, run it in jsdom or a real browser, and test fullstack server code in a separate Node project.

pages.title: Observability
pages.description: Report the errors your boundaries catch in production, follow a request from the server into the browser, and see what each user interaction cost, without wrapping a component.

pages.title: Build an observability adapter
pages.description: Connect an error monitor or a tracing SDK to a Solid app through the runtime's hooks and channels, with nothing wrapped, patched, or rewritten.

pages.title: From Solid 1.x
pages.description: Migrate a Solid 1.x application to Solid 2, including package imports, reactivity, effects, stores, async data, rendering, and tests.

pages.title: Data fetching from Solid 1
pages.description: Move Solid 1 data loading patterns to async computations one fetch at a time, and decide per fetch whether an update should wait, dim, or show a placeholder.

pages.title: From SolidStart
pages.description: Move a SolidStart 1 or released SolidStart 2 application to Solid 2 through @solidjs/vite-plugin start mode.

pages.title: From Solid Router 0.x/1.x
pages.description: Migrate JSX routes and the Solid Router 0.x/1.x data APIs to a Solid Router 2 createRouter instance.

pages.title: From Solid Meta 0.x
pages.description: Migrate your application from @solidjs/meta 0.x to 1.0.

pages.title: From React
pages.description: Map familiar React concepts to their closest Solid concepts, with equivalent examples and the semantic differences that matter during migration.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: Solid's own words, each defined in a few sentences and linked to the page that teaches it.

pages.title: Reference
pages.description: API reference for Solid: the reactive core, the web renderer, Solid Router, Solid Meta, the Vite plugin, and filesystem routing.

pages.title: solid-js
pages.description: Reference for the solid-js package: reactive primitives, stores, actions, context, flow components, and the public types.

pages.title: createEffect
pages.description: Creates a reactive effect with separate compute and effect phases.

pages.title: createMemo
pages.description: Creates a readonly derived reactive memoized signal.

pages.title: createOptimistic
pages.description: Creates an optimistic signal — a `Signal<T>` whose writes are tentative inside an `action`: they show up immediately, then auto-revert (or reconcile to the action's resolved value) once the pending work settles.

pages.title: createSignal
pages.description: Creates a simple reactive state with a getter and setter.

pages.title: flush
pages.description: Synchronously processes the pending reactive queue, or runs `fn` in a synchronous flush scope before draining the queue.

pages.title: isPending
pages.description: Returns whether the reactive reads inside `fn` depend on an in-flight value change that has not been revealed.

pages.title: latest
pages.description: Reads the freshest in-flight value available inside `fn`, falling back to the current settled value.

pages.title: untrack
pages.description: Runs `fn` outside of any reactive tracking — reads inside `fn` will not subscribe the current scope. Returns whatever `fn` returns.

pages.title: createOptimisticStore
pages.description: The store equivalent of `createOptimistic`.

pages.title: createProjection
pages.description: Creates a derived (projected) store — `createMemo` for stores. The derive function receives a mutable draft and either mutates it in place (canonical) or returns a new value.

pages.title: createStore
pages.description: Creates a deeply-reactive store backed by a Proxy. Reads track each property accessed; only the parts that change trigger updates.

pages.title: merge
pages.description: Merges multiple props-like objects into a single proxy that preserves reactivity.

pages.title: omit
pages.description: Returns a reactive proxy of `props` with the listed keys hidden. Tracking on the remaining keys is preserved.

pages.title: reconcile
pages.description: Creates a store setter callback that merges new data into the existing store by key.

pages.title: action
pages.description: The primitive for mutations: imperative async workflows whose writes span an async gap — optimistic write, server round-trip, reconciling write — where intermediate state must not leak and failure must revert cleanly (pair with `createOptimistic` / `createOptimisticStore`).

pages.title: affects
pages.description: Marks a reactive source or store location as pending while work that will change it is in flight.

pages.title: onSettled
pages.description: Schedules `callback` to run once after the reactive graph has fully settled — i.e. once every pending async read inside the current owner has resolved and the queue has flushed.

pages.title: refresh
pages.description: Invalidates one reactive source, forcing it to re-execute even if its inputs haven't changed, and returns a promise for the target's next settled state — the re-ask (and anything that supersedes it) has settled.

pages.title: until
pages.description: Awaits a reactive predicate and resolves the first time it becomes truthy, with the narrowed value.

pages.title: children
pages.description: Resolves a `children` accessor and exposes the result as an accessor with a `.toArray()` helper.

pages.title: createContext
pages.description: Creates a Context for sharing state with descendants of a Provider in the component tree.

pages.title: createUniqueId
pages.description: Returns a stable id string that matches between server-rendered and client-hydrated trees. Use it for `<label for>`, `aria-labelledby`, and other attributes that need consistent ids across SSR.

pages.title: lazy
pages.description: Defines a code-split component. The returned component triggers its dynamic import on first render and suspends through any enclosing `<Loading>` boundary while the chunk is in flight.

pages.title: useContext
pages.description: Reads the current value of a context.

pages.title: Errored
pages.description: Catches uncaught errors inside its subtree and renders fallback content instead.

pages.title: For
pages.description: Creates a list of elements from a list.

pages.title: Loading
pages.description: Renders a `fallback` while pending async reads inside the subtree settle.

pages.title: Repeat
pages.description: Creates a list of elements from a count.

pages.title: Reveal
pages.description: Coordinates the reveal timing of sibling `<Loading>` boundaries.

pages.title: Show
pages.description: Conditionally renders its children when `when` is truthy, otherwise renders the optional `fallback`.

pages.title: Switch / Match
pages.description: Switches between content based on mutually exclusive conditions. Renders the first `<Match>` whose `when` is truthy; falls back to `fallback` when none match.

pages.title: createRoot
pages.description: Creates a reactive root — an owner scope with its own `dispose()`.

pages.title: getObserver
pages.description: Returns the currently-tracking observer (the computation that subscribes to reactive reads at this point), or `null` if reads here would be untracked.

pages.title: getOwner
pages.description: Returns the current reactive owner — the lifecycle node that the next `cleanup()` / `onCleanup()` / `createSignal()` etc. Will be attached to.

pages.title: isDisposed
pages.description: Returns `true` when an owner has been disposed. Use it to ignore late work after the owner’s component or reactive scope has been removed.

pages.title: runWithOwner
pages.description: Executes `fn` with the given `owner` set as the current owner.

pages.title: createReaction
pages.description: Creates a reactive computation that runs after the render phase with flexible tracking.

pages.title: createRenderEffect
pages.description: Creates a reactive computation that runs during the render phase as DOM elements are created and updated but not necessarily connected.

pages.title: createTrackedEffect
pages.description: Creates a tracked reactive effect where dependency tracking and side effects happen in the same scope.

pages.title: onCleanup
pages.description: Low-level reactive-cleanup primitive. Registers a callback that runs when the surrounding owner is disposed.

pages.title: deep
pages.description: Subscribes the surrounding scope to every reachable level of a store value, then returns its plain view.

pages.title: isWrappable
pages.description: Returns whether a value would be wrapped in a store proxy.

pages.title: snapshot
pages.description: Returns the plain, unwrapped view of a store value without tracking, for serialization or for passing to code that must not observe the store.

pages.title: storePath
pages.description: x setter paths. Prefer draft-mutating store setters in new code.

pages.title: createErrorBoundary
pages.description: Lower-level primitive that backs the `<Errored>` flow control. Catches thrown errors inside `fn` and invokes `fallback(error, reset)` instead.

pages.title: createLoadingBoundary
pages.description: Lower-level primitive that backs the `<Loading>` flow control. Catches pending async reads inside `fn` and renders `fallback` until they settle.

pages.title: createRevealOrder
pages.description: Coordinate the reveal timing of sibling loading boundaries.

pages.title: mapArray
pages.description: Reactively maps an array, reusing the previously-mapped value for unchanged items.

pages.title: repeat
pages.description: Reactively renders a callback `count` times, reusing previously-rendered entries when only the count changes. Underlying helper for `<Repeat>`.

pages.title: Hydration
pages.description: Re-enables hydration within a `<NoHydration>` zone (passthrough on the client). Use it to opt a subtree back into hydration when the surrounding region was opted out.

pages.title: NoHydration
pages.description: Disables hydration for its children on the client. During hydration, skips the subtree entirely (returns undefined so DOM is left untouched).

pages.title: enableExternalSource
pages.description: Registers an adapter that lets Solid track reads from a non-Solid reactive system, such as MobX or Vue reactivity, inside its computations.

pages.title: flatten
pages.description: Resolves a children value to its renderable form: unwraps zero-arg functions (accessors), recursively flattens arrays, and optionally skips non-rendering values (`null`, `undefined`, `true`, `false`, `""`).

pages.title: NotReadyError
pages.description: Represents a read from an async reactive source before its first value is ready. Application code should normally let `Loading` and `Errored` boundaries handle this control flow.

pages.title: resolve
pages.description: Awaits a reactive expression and returns its first fully-settled value as a `Promise`.

pages.title: attribution / costs / feedback / formatOrigin / formatRerun / graphSize / subscriptions / why
pages.description: The attribution engine from `solid-js/attribution`: take a hold with `enable()`, read its interaction, navigation, hold, and re-run records on `OBSERVE.records.subscribe(type, …)` or from `history(type)`, and fold them with `costs()`, `feedback()`, `why()`, and `subscriptions()`.

pages.title: configureClientErrors
pages.description: Registers the ambient client error hook: called once per error object when an error boundary renders its fallback, with where the error was thrown and where it was met.

pages.title: DEV
pages.description: Dev tier (devtools hooks, graph traversal, console reporting): dev builds only.

pages.title: OBSERVE
pages.description: The observe tier's wiring: the records channel the runtimes and the attribution engine deliver on, the diagnostics channel, the attribution slot, `ownerPath()`, and on the server the trace-provider slot.

pages.title: Component / ComponentProps / FlowComponent / FlowProps / ParentComponent / ParentProps / Ref / ValidComponent / VoidComponent / VoidProps
pages.description: A general `Component` has no implicit `children` prop. If desired, specify one explicitly, e.g. `Component<{ name: string; children: Element }>`.

pages.title: Context / ContextProviderComponent
pages.description: Context API reference.

pages.title: JSX
pages.description: Selected public types from the `JSX` namespace. Element-specific attributes are available through `JSX.IntrinsicElements`.

pages.title: Owner
pages.description: Represents the owner of a reactive scope. Treat its structure as opaque and use the public owner APIs to inspect or run code in that scope.

pages.title: Accessor / Setter / Signal / SourceAccessor
pages.description: A zero-arg getter for a reactive value. Calling it inside a tracking scope (memo, effect compute, JSX expression) subscribes the scope to changes.

pages.title: Store / SolidStore
pages.description: A reactive view of a store's value. Update it through the paired `StoreSetter`.

pages.title: @solidjs/web
pages.description: Reference for @solidjs/web: DOM and HTML rendering, hydration, the head registry, DOM components, JSX properties, server functions, the request event, and the Performance panel tracks.

pages.title: clientOnly
pages.description: Creates a component that renders only in the browser. The server renders the fallback, and the client keeps that fallback through hydration before mounting the imported component.

pages.title: httpHeader
pages.description: Declares an HTTP response header (or with `append`, appends to one) for the lifetime of the current reactive scope during SSR — call it bare in a component or reactive-scope body.

pages.title: httpStatus
pages.description: Declares the HTTP response status (and optional status text) for the lifetime of the current reactive scope during SSR — call it bare in a component or reactive-scope body where the status is decided (a 404 route, an error fallback).

pages.title: hydrate
pages.description: Attaches a Solid component tree to server-rendered DOM and returns a function that disposes the hydrated tree.

pages.title: isDev
pages.description: Build-time constant that is `true` in development output and `false` in production output.

pages.title: isServer
pages.description: Build-time constant that is `true` in server output and `false` in browser output.

pages.title: renderToStream
pages.description: Streams an HTML response, flushing the synchronous shell first and then progressively emitting async-resolved fragments as their `<Loading>` boundaries settle.

pages.title: renderToString
pages.description: Renders a component tree synchronously to an HTML string. Async reads inside `<Loading>` boundaries emit their `fallback` content; for full-graph resolution await `renderToStream` instead.

pages.title: render
pages.description: Renders a component tree into a DOM element. Returns a dispose function that tears the tree down and cleans up reactive scopes when called.

pages.title: useHead
pages.description: Registers one or more head tag descriptors with Solid's ambient head registry.

pages.title: HeadTag
pages.description: Describes a tag registered with Solid's ambient head registry.

pages.title: dynamic
pages.description: Creates a stable component whose rendered component comes from a reactive source. The source can return a component, an intrinsic element name, a promise, or no component.

pages.title: Portal
pages.description: Renders its children into a different part of the DOM (modal roots, tooltips, layers that need to escape an `overflow: hidden` ancestor).

pages.title: ref
pages.description: Receives a DOM element or composes several callbacks that apply behavior to it.

pages.title: class
pages.description: Sets static and conditional class names from strings, objects, or nested arrays.

pages.title: style
pages.description: Sets an element's inline styles from a CSS string or an object of declarations.

pages.title: textContent
pages.description: Writes plain text as an element's complete contents through an optimized text-only path.

pages.title: innerHTML
pages.description: Parses an HTML string as an element's complete contents.

pages.title: Server functions
pages.description: Reference for Solid's server-function declarations, transport, and host integration.

pages.title: parseServerFunctionActionUrl / serverFunctionActionUrl / serverFunctionUrl
pages.description: Reads the function id back out of a server-rendered action url.

pages.title: configureServerFunctionsClient
pages.description: Configures the browser server-function endpoint, codec, request preparation, and response integration.

pages.title: GET
pages.description: Declares that a server-function read can use HTTP GET. Calls use a cacheable URL when the encoded arguments fit and fall back to a read-only POST when they do not.

pages.title: configureServerFunctionsServer / handleServerFunctionRequest
pages.description: Configures request scoping, invocation policy, result transforms, no-JavaScript handling, origin checks, and codecs for server functions.

pages.title: getServerFunctionInvocation
pages.description: Returns the identity of the server function that is currently executing.

pages.title: invoke
pages.description: Calls a server function with invocation-scoped `signal`, `keepalive`, or `priority` options.

pages.title: live
pages.description: Declares a server function whose async iterable represents one value that changes over time.

pages.title: withMeta / getServerFunctionMetadata / isServerFunction
pages.description: Attaches declaration metadata to a server-function reference and returns the reference.

pages.title: createNoJSHandler
pages.description: Creates the default response handler for browser form submissions made without the client runtime.

pages.title: enableRichArguments
pages.description: Enables codec encoding for server-function arguments that JSON cannot preserve.

pages.title: decodeResponse / registerFlightDataSource / subscribeFlightData
pages.description: Decodes a server-function response, including response envelopes and single-flight payloads.

pages.title: Request and response
pages.description: Reference for request context, response metadata, cookies, redirects, and errors.

pages.title: configureServerErrors
pages.description: Registers the ambient server error hook: called once per error object for every failure the server runtime handles or fails on, with the site that met it; the return value, when given, replaces what the client receives.

pages.title: parseCookieHeader / serializeCookie
pages.description: Parses a `Cookie` request header into a name → value map.

pages.title: getRequestEvent
pages.description: Returns the request event for the current server render, middleware chain, or server-function call.

pages.title: getTraceContext
pages.description: The trace the current request belongs to — continued from the incoming W3C `traceparent` when there was one, originated by the runtime otherwise; in observe/dev builds, merged with the installed provider's answer (`OBSERVE.server.trace`).

pages.title: provideRequestEvent
pages.description: Runs a callback in a server request-event scope backed by `AsyncLocalStorage`.

pages.title: redirect / isHref
pages.description: Creates a redirect `Response` (status 302 by default). Pass `revalidate` to name the cache keys the mutation invalidated so the client refetches them after following the redirect.

pages.title: reload
pages.description: Creates an empty `Response` that asks the client to revalidate the named cache keys without navigating.

pages.title: respond / isResponseEnvelope
pages.description: A value paired with response metadata (status, headers, `revalidate`) — for the things a naked return can't express.

pages.title: markSafeError / isSafeError
pages.description: Marks `error` as safe to serialize to the client verbatim, opting it out of production error sanitization (see `handleServerFunctionRequest`).

pages.title: enablePerformanceTracks
pages.description: Paint the attribution engine's records — and the web runtime's server-function `call` and `frame` records, with the server's own timing for each response under them (its `Server-Timing` metrics, placed by the browser's resource timing; the document's at enable) — as tracks in the Chrome Performance panel, from now until the returned function is called.
